narrative.title: Cipher Consistency Audit
narrative.scenario: A cipher vault replaces each plaintext letter with a ciphertext letter through a fixed substitution table, and an auditor receives two transcripts claimed to be encodings of the same message. The substitution must be consistent: one source letter always becomes the same target letter, and no two different source letters may collapse onto the same target. The auditor certifies the pair only when such a flawless mapping exists.
narrative.inputFormat: Two strings s and t of equal length.
narrative.outputFormat: true when the characters of s can be replaced to produce t under a consistent one-to-one mapping, false otherwise.
constraints: s and t consist of lowercase English letters

testCases.explanation: e maps to a and g maps to d; both replacements hold at every occurrence.
The two o's in s would need to become a and r simultaneously, which no single mapping allows.

hintLevels: Level 1: A valid remap is a two-way contract — every letter on the left names exactly one letter on the right, and vice versa.
Level 2: Walk both strings in lockstep with two dictionaries (left-to-right and right-to-left); any position where an existing entry disagrees fails the audit.
Level 3: The sneaky failure is a collision, not a mismatch — two left letters reaching the same right letter passes a one-way map check, so the reverse map (or a set of used targets) is mandatory.
